title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 55
paragraphs: When Xerxes had done this, they began to cross. The whole army, both foot and horse, went by one bridge — the one on the Pontus side — while the pack animals and servants went by the other, which was on the Aegean side. First the ten thousand Persians led the way, all wearing wreaths, and after them came the mixed contingents of the army made up of all kinds of nations — these crossed that day. On the next day, first the cavalry and those who carried their spears point-downward, also wearing wreaths; after them the sacred horses and the sacred chariot; and then Xerxes himself, with his spear-bearers and the thousand horsemen; and after them the rest of the army. Meanwhile the ships too put out from shore and crossed to the other side. I have heard, however, another account, that the king crossed very last of all.
